title: Time over noise: Asynchrony unlocks robust coordination beyond behavioural fluctuations — code and data archive
description:
Reference implementation, simulation pipeline, analysis routines, figure-generation scripts, and processed simulation outputs supporting the paper:

Sasai, K., Soga, Y. & Gunji, Y.-P. Time over noise: Asynchrony unlocks robust coordination beyond behavioural fluctuations. Nature Communications (2026).

The repository implements two decentralised update regimes on the distributed graph-colouring problem: the Synchronous Noise Model (SNM, behavioural noise via state-selection ε) and the Asynchronous Random Model (ARM, partial asynchrony coupled with gridlock-triggered random reselection). Includes the avalanche / spectral diagnostics used in the manuscript and the processed .pkl outputs for every figure.

Contents: source code (Python, NumPy / Numba / PyTorch GPU paths), experiment runners, figure scripts, supplementary diagnostics, and gzip-compressed pickle archives of all simulation outputs (~5 GB compressed).

Compressed pickle archives (.pkl.gz) reproduce the figures of the manuscript; uncompress with `gunzip` before use. See README.md and docs/reproduction.md for the figure-to-runner-to-data mapping.
